name: Overtone Singer
description: A narrow resonance that steps through the harmonics of a root note and sings a whistled melody out of a drone or a pad, the way an overtone singer does.

params.name: Root
params.description: The note whose harmonics the resonance sings. Set it to the key or to the drone of what is playing and the melody is always in tune with it.

params.name: Octave
params.description: Which octave the root sits in. Low octaves give a deep melody of close harmonics, high ones a thin bright whistle.

params.name: Low
params.description: The lowest harmonic the melody visits. Low numbers are wide leaps like a bugle call, higher ones lie as close as a scale.

params.name: High
params.description: The highest harmonic the melody visits. Raise it for a longer scale that climbs further into the whistle.

params.name: Pattern
params.description: How the resonance moves over its harmonics. Up and down climbs and returns, Wander drifts to a neighbour, Leap jumps anywhere and Hold stays where it is.

params.name: Pace
params.description: How often the resonance moves to another harmonic. Slow is a held tone that shifts now and then, fast is a running melody.

params.name: Glide
params.description: How long each move takes. Short steps cleanly from note to note, long slides through everything between as a mouth slowly changes shape.

params.name: Focus
params.description: How narrow and strong the resonance is. Low is a broad vowel colour over several harmonics, high singles out one harmonic as a clear ringing whistle.

params.name: Drone
params.description: How much of the sound around the resonance is kept. Fully down, only the harmonic being sung is left.

params.name: Spread
params.description: How far the right side trails the left through the melody. At zero both sides sing together, fully up the right is always one note behind.

params.name: Mix
params.description: Balance between the untouched sound and the singing one.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit. Two state-variable band-passes in series per side on one harmonic of a root note, moved from harmonic to harmonic by a free-running seeded melody, over the dry sound, with the resonant part held under a share of the input's own level.
